messages:
maya: Ran canary with the new kernel-switch heuristics (v2) on chatstream. seeing weird tail hump — p95 up ~45ms, p99 +120ms during tiny burst windows. anyone else?
adrian: saw something similar on r3-experiments yesterday. looks like queueing + kernel flip-flop.
rui: profile traces line up with KV-cache miss spikes at the same times the kernel chooser flips. attaching trace id 0xABCDEF (inline).
maya: here's the canary config we used:
```
# canary config snapshot
batcher:
  target_mb: 4        # targets very small microbatches for streaming
  hysteresis_ms: 8    # lowered to be more responsive
kernel_chooser:
  prefer_fast: true
  switch_threshold: 0.15
```
sam: we lowered hysteresis in v2 to shave avg latency, but we might be causing rapid kernel switches under bursty tiny loads.
lorna: can you dump per-client queue lengths and queue wait histograms? i want to see whether small batches are piling up then flushing when kernel switches.
adrian: canary perf numbers i grabbed: before v2 streaming p95 ~68ms p99 ~200ms; after v2 streaming p95 ~113ms p99 ~320ms. large jump in tail.
maya: dashboard: https://dash/internal/perf/runs/1854321 (canary group-b) — the tail hump is very spiky.
eng-bot: deploy v2 rolled to canary (3 hosts in group-b) :rocket:
rui: synthetic replay: 1 rps/client x 200 clients. when kernel switches, KV miss ratio jumps ~2.3x and tail increases. hypothesis: kernel switch path invalidates some warmed state / JIT outputs -> extra work per token -> tail.
sam: mitigation ideas: 1) add a cooldown window for kernel switches per model (avoid flip-flop), 2) increase hysteresis to 25ms for streaming, 3) limit microbatch max to 2 for streaming mode to avoid queue accumulation.
maya: plan proposal: run canary tomorrow with: cooldown=200ms, hysteresis 8->25, and enable kv-prefetch for short sequences. also enable tracing spans for kernel.switch and kv.prefetch. can we schedule?
lorna: +1 on traces. add span tags: model, host, queue_len, kernel_selected, kv_miss. we need to correlate events.
adrian: i'll own the canary rollout and collect per-host p95/p99 + queue histograms + kernel.switch counts. will post condensed results here.
ci-bot: canary scheduled: 1854321200 -> 1854321500 on hosts group-b (automated)
sam: also test identical total throughput for non-streaming completions — historically they didn't show the hump. if they diverge, it's an interaction between microbatching policies and streaming flush paths.
maya: agreed — we need a chatstream-specific microbatch cap if this holds.
adrian: starting synthetic runs now, will paste numbers after 10m.
adrian: quick results: streaming (same load) p95=110ms p99=320ms; non-streaming p95=70ms p99=90ms. so big divergence on tails.
maya: that's large. suggests streaming prefix flushing + kernel swap causes headroom collapse on a few hosts during bursts.
rui: filed perf issue #4321 with traces + flame graphs. linking: https://issues/internal/4321
maya: thanks all. sync tomorrow 10:00am PST to decide rollback vs tweak. :thumbsup:
